summary: Wilhelm Grube worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied under Vasily Vasiliev (~1874–1878) and Georg von der Gabelentz at Leipzig University (~1878–1881), later serving as an associate professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1892–1908).

Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1968–1970), the University of Hamburg (1981–1982), the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1989–1990), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1973–2000).

Wilhelm Pertsch worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber in 1850, at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1854), and under Rudolf von Roth (~1854–1855).
Wilhelm Printz was an Indologist and linguist. Between ~1924 and 1941, he served at the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft and as a professor at its library.

Wilhelm Rau worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Leipzig University (~1952–1953), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1955–1957 as professor), and the University of Marburg (~1957–1988 as professor).

Wilhelm Scherer specialized in linguistics. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1858–1860), he held posts at the University of Vienna (~1868–1872) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1877–1886).

Wilhelm Schulze worked in linguistics and Indology. He held posts at the University of Marburg (~1892–1895), the University of Göttingen (~1895–1902), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902–1932 as professor), succeeding Johannes Schmidt.

Wilhelm Streitberg was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig University (~1884–1888). He held posts at the University of Münster (~1899–1909), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1909–1920), and Leipzig University (~1920–1925).
Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1824–1827) and held a post at the University of Basel (~1833–1869).

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Frankfurt an der Oder, Göttingen, and Jena, and under Franz Bopp, founding Humboldt University of Berlin in 1810 after holding a post there (~1809–1810).
Will B. Miller specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~2007–2013), studying under Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Anne E. Monius.

Will Sweetman works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University (~1990–1993) and the University of Cambridge (~1994–1999), and held a post at the University of Otago (~2005).

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1951–1955), Princeton University (~1955–1962), and Harvard University, and held a post at the University of Toronto (~1971–1999).
Willard J. Peterson specializes in Sinology and history/archaeology. Mentored by Denis Twitchett, he served as a professor at Princeton University (~1971–2013).

Willard Van Orman Quine worked in philosophy and linguistics. Educated at Oberlin College and Harvard University, he served in the U.S. Navy (1942–1945) and held posts at Harvard (1933–1978) and Wesleyan University (1964–1965).

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University and the University of Hamburg. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and as a lecturer and professor at Heidelberg University from 1975.

Willem Caland worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Leiden University (~1877–1882), he held posts at Utrecht University as Chair of Sanskrit (1906–1929) and at Leiden University (1913–1914).

Willem van der Molen works in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1978–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William C. Kirby specializes in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Dartmouth College (~1968–1972) and Harvard University (~1972–1981), later holding a post at Harvard University (~1992).

William Carey worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Golok Nath Sharma in 1794, founded the Serampore Mission Press, and served as Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College (1801–1830).
